Agreed: no start time in ToolUse props, so measure around next(e) with the mod clock (it includes approval waits); ToolUse has no ctrl+o signal, so the raw view is the /tool-rows toggle; Bash has no numeric exit code and the error text has no guaranteed format, so parse it when present and else show no code. payload.text: Result 2026-10-08, Claude Code 2.1.295, scratch plugin hook-probe on tmux -L handily-live. (1) A repo with .pre-commit-config.yaml: no question, a refusal that names the manager, no hook written. (2) Inside a mod, git config --get core.hooksPath returns /dev/null although the shell returns nothing: Claude Code disables hooks for the git commands a mod runs. So a mod must not read core.hooksPath or --git-path hooks/pre-commit through its own git calls; read .git/config or use --git-common-dir. With /dev/null ignored the ask appeared once (Not now default, Install for this repo). (3) git rev-parse --git-path hooks/pre-commit gave no usable path inside the mod, so the install failed; the probe still kept the answer install and does not retry: the real mod must keep the answer only after the install works, or reinstall when the hook file is missing. (4) The builder ran the hook in a clone: an unrelated commit passed, a change or delete of an approved test was refused with the file named. (5) Install routes, measured by the builder: npm lefthook 2.2.1 runs from node_modules/.bin with no global install, but its postinstall runs lefthook install in INIT_CWD, so install with --ignore-scripts; uvx pre-commit 4.6.2 needs uv and a uv-managed Python, and uvx pre-commit install writes a uv cache Python path into the hook, which a cache clean breaks. (6) API gaps: $.fs.write has no file mode (chmod needs $.process.run), $.fs has no delete, AskOptions has no default (the first option acts as it), $.plugin has no data folder. Verdict: a plugin can install a test lock with consent; a plain hook script with no hook manager is the most robust route.
